Less is More Part 63 – Half-Hearted Cuisine
Apr 2013 • Friends
My Vietnamese colleagues are very obliging. When they know I am going to be in town, they will try to find a new restaurant for us to try. Sometimes I will also suggest something I came across on the internet eg. TA. (Needless to say there have been hits and misses.) So when I proposed Luc Bat, they collectively released an "incredulous gasp" - this place had never appeared on their radar. Unfazed, we went for mid-week dinner. It was empty - not a good sign.

Located on an incredibly narrow street which is barely wide enough for a car to pass through, we decided to sit upstairs. When the staff has to turn on the lights and fan as you go up, its yet another not-so-promising sign. I left it to the 'locals' to order what they deemed to be the house specials. Luc Bat is supposed to feature "mountain" ie. minority cuisine. We ordered five dishes to share - beef hotpot (good broth, tough meat), sweet sour frog (nice sauce, bony amphibians), pickled morning glory (interesting preparation), sausages (acquired taste, gamey), beef la lot (well-grilled, fibrous). None really stood out. Somehow the dishes just lacked enthusiasm. The service did not make much of an impression either - they did their job and that was it. Perhaps this was meant to be a drinking place cos the local wine was actually quite good and the food was merely an after-thought. As convivial as the environment was for a get-together among friends, I will probably not recommend you eat here unless you are too inebriated to go elsewhere.

A place of ALL in ONE
Feb 2013 • Friends
In contrast with the busy crisscrossed Old Quarter of Hanoi, when you enter Luc Bat, the peaceful atmosphere of the old architecture from French colony time and way they decor makes you feel a lot more than you coming for foods, but for the rich culture of Vietnam. Talking to the manager Huy - a very young professional owning this restaurant for the fun of meeting people and gathering friends- he would explain you the tales behind each picture on the wall. 

There are quite varieties in the menu at reasonable prices. You can find chicken or beef or pork cooked in so many ways, very traditional Vietnamese which you never find in other countries. 

My favorite here is Hotpot, each time coming here i tried different types. You must try also the sticky rice dish ''Xoi xeo''...yummy yummy, and the fresh roll ''Banh trang cuon thit ba chi''.

There are few dishes will surprise you, like...banana's flower salad..At first i thought ''How the hell people eat banana flower'', but believe me, its awesome. Try for yourself. 

About staff, not all of them speak good English, but they are quite friendly, they would use their body language to explain you whatever you concern, and sometimes it turns out to be quite funny.

People might have different opinions about this restaurant, I have no argument with that. Different people - different tastes. But I myself felt in love with this place from the first time i came.

Out-standing authentic cuisines
Dec 2012 • Friends
Location, atmospheres - unique: Tuck away in a small lane from the busiest area - Hanoi’s old quarters, with the early 1900s French architect styles, "Lục Bát" the name of the restaurant is also a traditional Vietnamese verse that formed the rhyme in Vietnamese poetry. 
The food - great: We have tried and been amazed by the signature dishes that are popular in the North and some ethnics mountain areas like dried mountainous Buffalo, grilled Mán northwest tribal piglet, Grilled chicken with Vietnamese strawberry leaves, simmerred frog with green banana and tofu..
The drink - impressive: The Northern Vietnamese’s special fermented glutinous rice wine has its own unique tastes, we found it more subtle, enriched with flavor of seasonal carefully selected glutinous grains than some of the East Asia’s ones like Shochu or Sake. It really goes well with the foods. For a moment, we felt like being immerged with Vietnamese culture, authentic foods and drink.

Conclusion: A touch of the soul of Vietnamese's culture and people that's unforgettable.

what HERITAGE cuisine is all about
Jan 2013 • Friends
I would not say this place serves the best cuisine in Hanoi, because it depends each people's taste. But I would say this is the place where you can taste, see and feel how Vietnamese people from small mountainous villages used to eat (they still do actually =)). From the meat to hotpot, from tea to wine, they serve only the ingredients which were caught, raised in the farms, on the mountain, in order to make the customers feel the wildness of Vietnamese cuisine.

For example, I ordered one dish called "kitchen's roof hang buffalo meat" (forgive my English =)). This meat was made in a way that I've never imagined. They roll and tight the buffalo meat tightly. And then, they hang it on the wall right next to the cooker. The heat from daily cooking will semi-cook it. At first, I felt weird tasting this. But then, the more I eat, the more I want...

Another favourite thing from this restaurant, to me, is wine. You have to taste it yourself to have your own review.=)
